appearance_facts.location: May bar, rightmost position on the Month axis
appearance_facts.fact: The May bar is a dark red rectangle whose top edge sits just above the 10,000 gridline, far below every other bar; it is the shortest bar on the chart.

appearance_facts.location: Apr, Jan, Jun, Feb, Mar bars (left to right of May)
appearance_facts.fact: The other five bars reach roughly 29,500 (Apr), 40,000 (Jan), 17,500 (Jun), 20,000 (Feb), and 27,000 (Mar) MWh, all visibly much taller than May.

appearance_facts.location: Relative to labeled reference points on its own series
appearance_facts.fact: May's bar top lies below the 10,000 tick's next gridline and well below the 15,000 and 20,000 levels, placing it at the bottom of the series.

printed_facts.fact: Apr; Jan; Jun; Feb; Mar; May

public_definitions: Task scope: “Review the monthly solar generation dashboard and decide whether May should be handled as a standard low-output case or escalated as a critical low-output anomaly for this reporting cycle.”
Option 1: “Route May to standard low-output follow-up”
Option 2: “Escalate May to critical low-output anomaly review”
Option 3: “Send May to background monthly record filing”
uncertain: No explicit numeric threshold or policy table on the page defines the boundary between “standard low-output” and “critical low-output anomaly”; the routing decision must rely on the visual magnitude of May's bar relative to the other months.
The exact MWh value for May is not printed; it is read visually as slightly above 10,000 MWh.
